focus: Data visualization, statistics, statistical analysis, and reproducible scientific computing
title: From Scraped Records to Honest Visual Evidence
utility_title: csv-statistics: Reproducible summaries from a numeric CSV column
utility_use_case: A researcher has exported instrument readings to a CSV and needs a repeatable first-pass summary before building a visualization. Running the utility produces a JSON record that can be archived with the dataset or consumed by another script. The counts of missing and invalid cells make basic exclusions visible, while the seeded percentile bootstrap provides an uncertainty summary conditional on the observed values and the resampling assumptions. It is a descriptive workflow aid, not a hypothesis test or a causal analysis.

editorial_review.summary: Corrected the README to clarify which errors the utility reports through the argument parser and to disclose arithmetic overflow for extreme finite inputs.

edits.old: Errors are reported through the argument parser and result in a nonzero exit status.
edits.new: Argument errors and handled input errors are reported through the argument parser and result in a nonzero exit status.

edits.old: A seed cannot correct selection bias, and more resamples reduce Monte Carlo variability without fixing poor data.
edits.new: A seed cannot correct selection bias, and more resamples reduce Monte Carlo variability without fixing poor data. Extreme finite values can still cause arithmetic overflow during summary or resampling calculations.
